title: Stranglethorn Vale
body: Stranglethorn Vale is a vast, sweltering jungle at the southern end of the Eastern Kingdoms, once the heart of the Gurubashi Empire, whose ruined troll cities lie everywhere beneath the vines. What remains of the Gurubashi has splintered into warring tribes, and in the old capital, Zul'Gurub, the blood god Hakkar has been called back into the world. Outsiders come for the jungle's riches and dangers: big game hunters, Venture Company loggers, the soldiers of the mad Colonel Kurzen, the Horde at Grom'gol, and the goblins of Booty Bay, who trade with all comers while Bloodsail pirates prowl their waters.

title: Rebel Camp
body: Northwest of the road from Duskwood, a handful of soldiers hold a small camp under Lieutenant Doren. They once marched under Colonel Kurzen and served him with fierce loyalty, until his descent into corruption twisted that loyalty into rage and they broke away. Outnumbered ten to one by their former comrades, they live by guile: Sergeant Yohwa plans raids on the compound to the east, and Brother Nimetz searches troll legends for the cause of Kurzen's fall.

parts.body: Even here the rebels were not safe. Someone passed word of a secret mission to the enemy, and a muddy note signed only with an M led to the traitor: Private Merle, a soldier Doren had thought brave and true.

title: Nesingwary's Expedition
body: Beside a river inlet in northern Stranglethorn, near old docks left by some forgotten people, the dwarven big game hunter Hemet Nesingwary pitched the camp from which he hunted the Vale. His son, Hemet Nesingwary Jr., keeps it now with his father's old companions, and strangers must prove themselves against raptors, tigers and panthers before they may join the hunt. The elder Hemet has written up his adventures as a novel, The Green Hills of Stranglethorn.

parts.body: These days the elder Nesingwary hunts far from the Vale, gone off to more exotic lands in search of bigger prey.
The great beast that drew the younger Hemet to Stranglethorn is King Bangalash, a white tiger that has sent him crawling back to camp more than once.

title: Ruins of Zul'Kunda
body: Zul'Kunda is a sprawling troll ruin near the northern coast and the seat of the Bloodscalp tribe, one of the two great tribes left of the Gurubashi. Their chief, Gan'zulah, and his witch doctor, Nezzliok the Dire, rule from deep within, while headhunters stalk the ruins carrying the shrunken heads of their victims. The Bloodscalps are sworn enemies of the Darkspear and wage war on the Skullsplitters. Its ancient tablets tell of the fall of the empire.

title: Grom'gol Base Camp
body: Grom'gol is the Horde's walled stronghold on the western coast of Stranglethorn, held for the Warchief by Commander Aggro'gosh, and its first duty is to keep a chain of supply open to Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows. Zeppelins link it to Orgrimmar and the Undercity. Darkspear trolls serve here too, back in the jungle their tribe once called home, though the local tribes count the Darkspear as enemies.

title: Ruins of Zul'Mamwe
body: Zul'Mamwe lies in a mountain-ringed valley in the east of the Vale and is the stronghold of the Skullsplitters, the second great troll tribe of Stranglethorn and bitter rivals of the Bloodscalps. Their chief, Ana'thek the Cruel, holds the ruins with the witch doctor Mogh the Undying, and the tribe keeps piles of trophy skulls here and at the nearby ruins. Strangely, one of Kurzen's soldiers walks among them, his mind enslaved by Mogh.

title: Yojamba Isle
body: Off the northwestern coast lies Yojamba Isle, where envoys of the Zandalar tribe have made their camp. The Zandalari defeated the blood god Hakkar at Zul'Gurub in ages past, and now that he has risen there again they have returned to oppose him, calling on outsiders of every race to help. Molthor, the Hand of King Rastakhan, leads the expedition, and his people tend the Altar of Zanza and guard a captured Hakkari zealot.

parts.body: Once the way into Zul'Gurub lies open to outsiders, more of Rastakhan's envoys take up their posts on the isle, each dealing with heroes of a particular calling.

title: Gurubashi Arena
body: North of Booty Bay stands a great stone arena raised by the Gurubashi trolls, whose ancient fights were to the death and whose sand was stained with troll blood. The empire is gone but the bloodletting is not. A pirate called Short John Mithril presides over the sport now, leaving a chest of treasure on the arena floor from time to time for whoever can claim it, and rivals of every race gather to fight over the prize.

title: Ruins of Aboraz
body: Northeast of Booty Bay, the ruins of Aboraz and neighboring Jubuwal have become the domain of Zanzil the Outcast, a witch doctor exiled by his own people, who fear his power over the minds of others. He feeds a mixture of jungle plants to those who fall into his hands, leaving them strong of body and empty of will, and zombies, naga and trolls now serve him among the stones.

parts.body: Zanzil keeps a more precious captive among his followers: Yenniku, youngest son of the Darkspear chief, given to the Gurubashi long ago and lost when his tribe left the jungle, whom the witch doctor controls body and soul.

title: Booty Bay
body: Booty Bay is a goblin port built into the cliffs around Blackwater Cove at the tip of the cape. It belongs to the Steamwheedle Cartel and is ruled by Baron Revilgaz, whose Blackwater Raiders keep their seat atop the Salty Sailor Tavern. Every race is welcome so long as it brings coin and keeps the peace, and the town's bruisers fall hard on anyone who spills blood on neutral ground.

title: Wild Shore
body: The Wild Shore runs along the southern tip of the cape east of Booty Bay, and the Bloodsail Buccaneers, rivals of Booty Bay's Blackwater Raiders, have made it their base. Their camps teem with deckhands and swashbucklers, and just offshore ride three Bloodsail ships, the Crimson Veil, the Riptide and the Damsel's Luck, where Fleet Master Firallon commands from below decks. Those who have made themselves no friends of Booty Bay may find a welcome among the pirates.

parts.body: The orders kept on this shore held the Bloodsails' secret. From here they meant to strike at Booty Bay itself: ships closing in from the sea, guns pinning the harbor, a landing party putting the town to the torch, and the black spot on Revilgaz and Fleet Master Seahorn.
sources: quest 604 description (southern command post on the Wild Shore, charts and orders)

parts.body: Seahorn struck first, sending a small band of fighters to the pirates' landing spot, and Firallon and his captains were slain.

title: Colonel Kurzen
body: Colonel Kurzen was once a great and noble man, a soldier of Stormwind who led an expedition into Stranglethorn and whose men followed him with fierce loyalty. Somewhere in the jungle he fell into cruelty and madness, and his soldiers became its instruments. From a fortified compound of jungle fighters, medicine men and trained war beasts, he commands from deep within a cavern called the Stockpile, and even the rebels call him a brilliant tactician.

parts.body: Brother Nimetz believes the colonel did not fall on his own. His study of troll legends led him to Mai'Zoth, an ogre mage of the Mosh'Ogg mound who holds the Mind's Eye, a jewel rumored to bend minds.
sources: quest 207 description (once a great, noble man)

parts.body: Kurzen is dead, cut down deep within the Stockpile from which he commanded, and Lieutenant Doren's rebels can breathe easier at last.

title: Nimboya
body: Nimboya is a Darkspear troll sent from Orgrimmar back to Stranglethorn on a grim errand. As was his people's custom, his chief's youngest son, Yenniku, was given to the Gurubashi of Zul'Gurub, and when the Darkspear left the jungle with Thrall the boy was lost to them. Nimboya means to find him, and inspects the shrunken heads the Bloodscalps take in dread of finding Yenniku among them.

parts.body: Forced from the dead lips of the Bloodscalp witch doctor, the truth came out: the boy was taken by Zanzil the Outcast, who controls him body and soul.
sources: quest 581 description

parts.body: Kin'weelay of Grom'gol reshaped the Mind's Eye, taken from the ogre mage Mai'Zoth, into a soul gem; Yenniku's soul was drawn into it and carried back to Nimboya, freed from Zanzil's will.
